newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: CSM profits up 8.1 percent in first half.
newsitem.headline: CSM profits up 8.1 percent in first half.

text.p: Dutch food group CSM NV said on Thursday its net profits rose by 8.1 percent in the six months to end-March 1997 and forecast a further increase in the current second half year.

First half net profit increased to 101.1 million guilders ($53.1 million), from 93.5 million in the same period in 1995/1996. Turnover increased over 11 percent to 1.61 billion guilders, while operating profit grew nearly 12 percent to 148.8 million.
The net profit figure was at the low end of analysts' estimates, which had ranged from 100 to 106 million guilders.

"Based on the satisfactory course of business at the divisions, the contribution of acquisitions and the positive impact of changes in currency rates, CSM expects that net profits will show an increase in the second half as well," the company said in a statement.
The currency effect had contributed an extra 59 million guilders to turnover, translating into a near two percent boost to net profit, CSM said.
Turnover in its sugar division had been slightly lower than the previous year over the first half, the company said, but over the full year was expected to come out about the same.
In the food division, turnover and profits were expected to rise over the full year due to recent acquisitions.
The ingredients division was seen showing a strong turnover and profit rise over the current year, both as a result of acquisitions and through autonomous growth, CSM said.

CSM shares closed up 1.70 guilders at 110.40 guilders on the Amsterdam Stock exchange on Thursday. The half-year results were released after the close. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040 ($ = 1.903 Dutch Guilders)
